title: TREL: add conversation support (from DNS)
description: Heuristic dissector was not strong enough yet , so added some code which create conversation in `packet-dns.c` based on ip and port , because TREL port is broadcasted over `mdns-sd`(service discovery).

hi @JaapKeuter  i have added -1 to check if trel port is assigned or not, unlike previous implementation where static variable were assigned -1 ,and commented code is for future modification since TREL does not have strong heuristic dissection as of yet, once protocol is evolved enough it will be used. and conversation code in DNS file will be removed.

From the intent of the patch it seems, that you are replacing a heuristic dissector hookup with a static version of the port definition. This does not really fly for a few reasons:

* We try to avoid removing existing functionality, as people might be using it. Instead you could add configuration variables, which override the heuristic and allow for the use of a configured port
* static definitions do not work, especially if used globally. Instead, the correct way - if this is to be configured - is to use a preference variable which would allow the user to change it.
* Code that is simply commented out should be removed. Otherwise later code reviews might wonder why this code is present at all.

So no, in this version, the code cannot be merged, but if you address these issues, I think it might be mergable.
hi, new code i added have same functionality, so any user using existing code would have no effect , still anyway ill add configuration variable to disable the code.

also i didnt get this  static definitions do not work, especially if used globally. Instead, the correct way - if this is to be configured - is to use a preference variable which would allow the user to change it.,  what am is supposed to do here?
As mentioned before, the right choice here would be to let the user configure it via preference variable. We try to avoid static because "magic numbers" lead to issues that are hard to diagnose
hi, this was added make more reliable automatic TREL dissection. but since this does not adhere to standard ill be rolling back to previous version and this MR will be closed.

Additional question. Why is the heuristic dissector not strong enough? Would it be possible to make it stronger? Is there a specific use case it cannot catch, but could be addressed if the heuristic is adapted?

the reason is we have only specific fields to determine, which overlap with other protocols, like we saw one issue with DTLS, even though the packet was belonging to other protocol it was getting dissected as TREL , not a good thing.

So basically, you are getting too many false positives and instead of drilling down on why or hardening the heuristic, you instead disable the functionality. This is the wrong approach, the right one would be to fix the reason for the false positives. 

Either the approach in general is flawed and cannot be achieved via a heuristic dissector, or the current heuristic is not specific enough and too broadly tailored. If what you say is true, and there is simply no method to enable a good heuristic approach, then removing the functionality would be fine. But in this case it seems, that the protocol can be identified via an additional key, namely the name of the service. In such a case, reading that key, searching for the established prefix could give a stronger positive and help reduce the false positives (see https://openthread.io/reference/group/plat-trel?hl=de#otplattrelregisterservice). Or am I wrong here?

hi , in addition to above statement , TREL has only  this 

1. Version (TREL version)
2. RSV 
3. TREL packet type(0 broacast, 1 unicast, 2 Acknowledgment)
4. channel (IEEE 802.15.4 channel number)
5. 802.15.4 PAN ID
6. packet number
7. 802.15.4 Ext Src Addr

fields , which we used but still it gives false positive in heuristic dissection scenario ,  so will be manually disabling the protocol or adding port in preference variable will be used here, and this MR will be closed.
